format.critical_guard: Fail for an invented national vote, binding commitment, Council adoption, disclosure, or assigned card. An explicit uncertainty marker is acceptable when a card is unavailable. Report unsupported workshop conclusions separately from official-record fabrication.

units.required: Use the exact checked status in the first line.
Treat the status as the disposition of the hypothetical workshop, rather than an official vote or action.

Specify a compatible next step. Refer unresolved terms for another workshop round on impasse, propose the checked slot on agreement, or seek the missing card when unresolved. Semantically equivalent recommendations count.
Make clear what the chair or office can do: recommend or refer in Mali, propose or seek confirmation in Myanmar. No new Council authorization is implied.
Attribute the visible first card accurately to its owner, including its limit if it is exclusive.
Attribute the second card to its actual owner if delivered. If unavailable, identify that holder and state that its card is missing. Forwarding does not change authorship.
Explain why the observed preferences produce disjoint packages, establish the recommended common slot, or leave compatibility open.

State the concrete tradeoff or evidence gap. In a confirmed Mali impasse, the unresolved package choice is review versus closure. In the Myanmar agreement, the liaison's flexibility meets the UN office's early-only timing. In either unresolved case, the exact second-holder mandate or availability is still needed.

required.mali: Identify S/2023/638 as not adopted because of the negative vote by a permanent member, with tally 13–1–1.
required.myanmar: Identify resolution 2669 and its oral report to the Security Council in coordination with the ASEAN Special Envoy.

required.mali: Identify separate S/2023/639 as not adopted because it fell short of sufficient affirmative votes, with tally 1–1–13.
required.myanmar: Preserve the deadline of 15 March 2023 and link the oral report to UN support for the Five-Point Consensus.
